like_for_like.comparison_label: January through August 2026 compared with January through August 2025. This is not a full-year comparison.

tests.research_question: Do recorded monthly registration volumes differ by calendar month?
tests.null_hypothesis: The distribution of year-month registration counts is the same for every calendar month.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: At least one calendar month has a different distribution.
tests.variables: Response: registration count for one year-month. Factor: calendar month number.
tests.assumptions: Each observation is one year-month, not one registration transaction. The test does not assume a normal distribution. Year-months are treated as separate observations, although successive years are not fully independent. Low-volume months stay in this primary test.
tests.limitation: A difference between month distributions can reflect level changes across eras as well as a repeating within-year pattern. The year-normalized month shares are the descriptive check for a within-year pattern. This is not an anomaly-detection result.
tests.conclusion: The null hypothesis is not rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level.
tests.interpretation: The null hypothesis is not rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

tests.research_question: Does the calendar-month comparison change if the low-volume months are set aside?
tests.null_hypothesis: The distribution of the remaining year-month counts is the same for every calendar month.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: At least one calendar month still has a different distribution.
tests.variables: Same as the primary calendar-month test, after removing months below 10% of the median monthly count.
tests.assumptions: This is a sensitivity check. It is not in the Bonferroni family and it does not remove the months from the dataset.
tests.limitation: Setting unusual months aside changes the question being asked. The primary result keeps those months.
tests.conclusion: The unadjusted p-value is below 5%. This test is outside the Bonferroni family. The effect size is medium.
tests.interpretation: The unadjusted p-value is below 5%. This test is outside the Bonferroni family. The effect size is medium. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

tests.research_question: Does the annual share of recorded registrations classified as electric change monotonically across complete years?
tests.null_hypothesis: The Spearman rank correlation between year and annual electric registration share is zero.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: The rank correlation is not zero.
tests.variables: Paired observations are complete registration years. The share is electric registrations divided by that year's registrations.
tests.assumptions: The correlation describes a monotonic association. Partial years are excluded. Years are ordered but are not a random sample from a larger population of years.
tests.limitation: A rank correlation with year does not identify a cause. It does not estimate a future share.
tests.conclusion: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is large.
tests.interpretation: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is large. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

tests.research_question: Does the annual share of recorded registrations classified as hybrid change monotonically across complete years?
tests.null_hypothesis: The Spearman rank correlation between year and annual hybrid registration share is zero.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: The rank correlation is not zero.
tests.variables: Paired observations are complete registration years. Hybrid means hybrid_petrol or hybrid_diesel. Those fuel codes stay separate in the fuel tables.
tests.assumptions: Same design as the electric-share correlation. A partial latest year is excluded.
tests.limitation: A rank correlation with year does not identify a cause and is not a forecast.
tests.conclusion: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is large.
tests.interpretation: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is large. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

tests.research_question: Are annual registration volume and annual electric registration share associated across complete years?
tests.null_hypothesis: The Spearman rank correlation between annual registration count and annual electric share is zero.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: The rank correlation is not zero.
tests.variables: Complete years only. Volume is the annual registration count. Electric share uses that same year's count as the denominator.
tests.assumptions: Two-sided rank correlation. This association is not in the Bonferroni family because volume and electric share can move together through a shared time trend.
tests.limitation: An association between volume and electric share is not evidence that one produces the other. Both can follow the same time order.
tests.conclusion: The unadjusted p-value is below 5%. This test is outside the Bonferroni family. The effect size is large.
tests.interpretation: The unadjusted p-value is below 5%. This test is outside the Bonferroni family. The effect size is large. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

tests.research_question: Does the fuel-category composition of recorded registrations differ between 2017-2019 and 2023-2025?
tests.null_hypothesis: Fuel category and period are independent in the included categories.
tests.alternative_hypothesis: Fuel category and period are not independent.
tests.variables: Counts of registration transactions in two windows of complete years. Each window is three years. The windows are 2017-2019 and the latest three complete years when both exist. 2020 and 2021, which contain the low-volume months, are outside both windows. The partial latest year is outside both windows.
tests.assumptions: Expected counts must be at least 5. Categories that break that rule are omitted from the test and listed. They remain in the descriptive fuel table. No continuity correction is applied. Omitted from the test: diesel_ng, ng, hydrogen, greendiesel_ng, other.
tests.limitation: The sample size is a count of registration transactions, so a small composition difference can produce a very small p-value. Practical reading uses Cramér's V and the change in shares. The test does not say why the composition differs, and it does not merge the omitted fuel codes into another code.
tests.conclusion: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is small.
tests.interpretation: The null hypothesis is rejected at the Bonferroni-adjusted 5% level. The effect size is small. Statistical significance is separate from practical importance. The effect-size label uses conventional benchmarks only as a reading aid.

phase5: A candidate forecasting target is the monthly count of recorded registrations from 2000-01-02 through 2026-08-31. The grain is one month. The series includes every channel and the low-volume months.
2026 is observed through August and is a partial year. A later model should not treat that year as a full year equal to the previous full year. This phase does not extend it to a full-year figure.
Calendar month is not supported as a strong feature by the primary test.

The national monthly count mixes geographic registration offices and the Rakan Niaga channel. Rakan Niaga accounts for 42.3% of recorded registrations in the full series. Its share in 2014 and in the latest complete year should be read from the annual channel table before a later model treats the national series as one stable process.

A second candidate target is the monthly count of registrations classified as electric. The first complete year with an electric registration in this snapshot is 2009. Early years are sparse. Electric share is a composition of recorded registrations, not a measure of consumer adoption.
The rank correlations of electric share and hybrid share with year are exploratory. They do not mean a later model should use year as its main predictor of registration volume.

Annual electric share, fuel-category share, and manufacturer share are not adopted as forecasting predictors. Any later use would need a time-ordered evaluation and a leakage check. An association with registration volume is not evidence that one series causes the other.
Low-volume months remain in the series. A later model has to decide how to treat them with that limitation stated, rather than dropping them silently.
